standard_prerequisites.name: Tor amplitude in an interval
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the definition of tor amplitude of an object of D(O) via the vanishing of Tor_O^q(K, F) outside an interval for all O-modules F
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the additivity of the Tor functors that makes the one-line proof valid.

core_obligations: Recall that the Tor functors are additive (proof line 12611): for the direct sum K + L, Tor_O^q(K + L, F) = Tor_O^q(K, F) + Tor_O^q(L, F).
If K + L has tor amplitude in [a, b], then each Tor_O^q(K, F) and Tor_O^q(L, F) is zero outside [a, b] (proof line 12611), which is exactly that K and L each have tor amplitude in [a, b].
proof_roadmap: Tor is additive over direct sums.
A direct-sum object of tor amplitude [a, b] has all its Tor's vanishing outside [a, b], hence so do the summands individually.
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the additivity observation for tor amplitude (statement lines 12603-12608). The proof (proof lines 12610-12612) is the single sentence that the Tor functors are additive: Tor of K + L with any F splits as Tor(K, F) + Tor(L, F), so vanishing outside the interval for the sum forces the same vanishing for each summand. H2: immediate from additivity of Tor.
